task: P1 -- profile the RDR green-screen state (step 1: where does the time go)
method: perf record -g (frame-pointer, 30 s) + perf record -g --call-graph dwarf (15 s), both on the live guest; /usr/lib/linux-tools-6.8.0-149/perf; plus a 1 Hz /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat sampler and exact guest-log window counting

run.green_onset: 92 s after the chapter card; green_frac 0.8740 -> 0.9063 (test G>60,R<40,B<40)
run.profiled_state_confirmed_green: all 34 sampler frames during the profile measure green_frac 0.906

findings.title_progresses: YES, slowly: 60 flips per 34.210 s = 1.75 fps on the green, against 29.97 fps on the loading card (17x slower). Not frozen.
findings.lifted_guest_code_share: 0.30% of 18124 samples (54 samples over 8 distinct f_XXXXXXXX, max 3 each)
findings.interpreter_total: ~33% of all samples is the SPU interpreter and its bookkeeping; the bookkeeping alone (19.92%) costs more than twice the instruction emulation (9.07%)
findings.cpu: 615% across 47 threads; guest main thread is 7.2%; six SPU threads ~99% each + RSX FIFO 97.8% (87.7% of that is its own idle-wait, 0 semaphore waits/s)
findings.fibres: CreateFiber 5.24/s, RunFibers 1.77/s, JoinFiber 5.30/s, 9098 switches/s, 5148 switches per RunFibers call (two independent methods agree within 1%)
findings.file_io: 0 fs: read fd lines/s on the green with PS3BASE_FS_LOG=1 set -- the load is genuinely finished

not_measured: RAGE script opcodes/s: not countable without instrumenting (forbidden), and the interpreter f_00d19278 has 0 samples in both profiles, so there is nothing to count. Substituted the runtime's own 'main: pgw' guest-write counter (falls from ~100/s to ~31/s).
harness_defects_found_and_fixed: tools/green_screen_probe.sh starts TWO game instances: it launches $BIN itself (lines 27-30) and then drive_rdr.py launches it again in run().
kill (SIGTERM) of drive_rdr.py lets its finally block SIGKILL the guest, so no guest is left to profile; SIGKILL the driver instead.

The probe's solid-screen test uses %[fx:standard_deviation] as if it were 0..255; it is 0..1, so the threshold matches every frame. My first run profiled the red chapter card because of this; that run is discarded and not reported.
